meta.title: Youtarr Jellyfin Quick Connect setup authentication
meta.author: Codex manager council

feature.problem_statement: Youtarr v0.3.29 setup asks the browser for an editable Jellyfin server URL and a password even though the deployment already has a configured internal endpoint. This creates target-confusion risk and an unnecessary password path for a VPN-only service. Jellyfin Quick Connect provides a user-approved, short-lived code flow that can authenticate a per-user setup session without putting the Quick Connect secret in the browser.
goals: Make server-orchestrated Jellyfin Quick Connect the default Youtarr setup authentication flow.
Keep the Quick Connect secret server-side and bind completion to one opaque browser flow and one immutable Jellyfin user ID.
Provide an explicit password fallback without any editable server URL field.
Expose only a separately configured, validated browser-facing Jellyfin link while keeping the internal service URL private.
Deliver a testable, VPN-only, per-user implementation with chart/config/GitOps/release/rollout requirements.
non_goals: Changing Jellyfin server settings or automatically approving a Quick Connect code for a user.
Accepting arbitrary Jellyfin URLs, proxy targets, redirects, or credentials from the browser.
Persisting a Jellyfin password, Quick Connect secret, Jellyfin session token, or browser local-storage credential.
Supporting backwards compatibility for the editable server_url setup contract; this is an intentional breaking change.
Replacing Youtarr's existing Google setup flow or implementing a general identity provider.
scope_in: Youtarr public setup API, embedded setup UI, Jellyfin client, session/flow persistence, tests, and API documentation.
Quick Connect Initiate, polling via Connect, and final AuthenticateWithQuickConnect behavior using stable headers.
Password fallback against configured internal Jellyfin URL with immutable user-ID session binding.
Separate internal and browser URL configuration validation, chart values/templates, VPN-only ingress/network policy, GitOps image/release/rollout documentation, and Playwright acceptance.
scope_out: Live Jellyfin or Kubernetes mutation during this spec stage.
Admin-token routes, worker routes, or unrelated Youtarr account/subscription behavior.
Public internet exposure, non-VPN authentication, or user-selected Jellyfin server discovery.
A fallback that stores reusable password credentials or Quick Connect secrets.

requirements.statement: The setup UI MUST present Quick Connect as the default Jellyfin authentication action and MUST present password authentication only as an explicit fallback action; the UI MUST remove editable server URL input.
requirements.rationale: The configured deployment target is authoritative and Quick Connect should be the least-secret default.

requirements.statement: The controller MUST use only a validated configured internal Jellyfin URL for all server-to-server calls and MUST reject missing, malformed, non-http(s), hostless, or otherwise invalid internal configuration before serving authentication.
requirements.rationale: Browser input must never select an outbound target and startup must fail closed.

requirements.statement: The deployment MUST configure a separate browser-facing Jellyfin URL, validate it independently at startup, and expose only that fixed safe link or a fixed Jellyfin Quick Connect destination; no request field may override it and the internal URL MUST NOT appear in browser responses or UI source.
requirements.rationale: Users need a link to approve in Jellyfin without leaking cluster-internal topology or enabling open redirects.

requirements.statement: Quick Connect initiation MUST call the official Jellyfin POST /QuickConnect/Initiate endpoint through the internal client and MUST send a stable, documented X-Emby-Authorization client/device header containing a stable Youtarr app name, device name, device ID, and version.
requirements.rationale: Jellyfin requires the official flow and stable client identity for auditability and device recognition.

requirements.statement: After initiation, the controller MUST retain the Quick Connect Secret only server-side (preferably hashed or encrypted at rest), return only a six-character user code, expiry/status metadata, and the fixed browser link, and MUST never put Secret in HTML, JavaScript, JSON, cookies readable by script, query strings, logs, errors, metrics, or tracing.
requirements.rationale: The secret is the capability used to obtain authentication information and must not cross the browser boundary.

requirements.statement: Each pending Quick Connect flow MUST have an unpredictable opaque HttpOnly Secure SameSite flow cookie or state bound to the current browser session, immutable Youtarr session identity, and initiating user context; the client MUST poll a same-origin endpoint without page redirect or provider callback.
requirements.rationale: Opaque state prevents flow swapping and keeps the UI in control of progress without exposing capability material.

requirements.statement: The controller MUST poll the official GET /QuickConnect/Connect?secret= endpoint server-side until pending, authenticated, expired, canceled, or error; polling MUST use bounded intervals and deadlines, return sanitized states, and MUST never return the upstream secret or raw response.
requirements.rationale: The browser should not poll Jellyfin directly and upstream failures must not become data leaks.

requirements.statement: A flow MUST expire after ten minutes, be single-use on successful completion or explicit cancel, reject reuse and cross-session polling, and enforce rate limiting separately for initiation, polling, password attempts, and cancel operations with sanitized Retry-After behavior.
requirements.rationale: Short lifetime, one-time consumption, and bounded attempts limit replay and abuse.

requirements.statement: The user MUST explicitly approve the displayed code in an already-authenticated Jellyfin client; once approved, Youtarr MUST call POST /Users/AuthenticateWithQuickConnect with only the server-side Secret and MUST derive the immutable Jellyfin user ID from the authenticated result.
requirements.rationale: Quick Connect is an approval flow, not a silent account takeover, and the Jellyfin Id is the stable binding key.

requirements.statement: On completion, Youtarr MUST create or reuse exactly the session record bound to jellyfin:<immutable-Jellyfin-Id>, must not bind by username or display name, and every session/status/subscription operation MUST predicate data access on that immutable ID.
requirements.rationale: Names can change or collide; cross-user data isolation requires an immutable identity predicate.

requirements.statement: Password fallback MUST send username and password only to the configured internal Jellyfin endpoint via AuthenticateByName, MUST clear request/body/UI password material immediately after use, MUST never persist or log the password or returned Jellyfin token, and MUST bind the resulting session exactly as Quick Connect does.
requirements.rationale: Fallback is necessary but must have no durable secret or target-selection surface.

requirements.statement: All mutating setup endpoints (initiate, poll state transitions, authenticate completion, cancel, fallback login, disconnect, and logout as applicable) MUST enforce the existing opaque session plus CSRF behavior, and cookies MUST be Secure, HttpOnly where appropriate, SameSite, scoped to the setup origin/path, and non-persistent beyond configured session TTL.
requirements.rationale: Quick Connect does not remove CSRF or session fixation requirements.

requirements.statement: The implementation MUST define and test restart, duplicate initiation, stale flow, expired flow, explicit cancel, Jellyfin disabled/unreachable, malformed upstream, wrong-session, wrong-user, rate-limited, and browser-close cases; all failure responses MUST be generic and safe.
requirements.rationale: Authentication state machines fail at boundaries and must fail closed without leaking secrets.

requirements.statement: The Helm chart and GitOps manifests MUST configure distinct internal and browser URLs, public listener/ingress exposure only through the VPN/Tailscale path, NetworkPolicy restrictions, secret references without plaintext credentials, health checks, immutable image digest, and a documented staged rollout, rollback, and release promotion procedure.
requirements.rationale: Configuration and network policy are part of the security boundary and must be reproducible.

requirements.statement: Browser-facing validation MUST use Playwright only and MUST exercise the VPN-only deployed setup UI for Quick Connect approval, polling completion, fixed link safety, password fallback, CSRF/session expiry, and two-user isolation; direct HTTP calls, curl, Selenium, or Cypress MUST NOT substitute for UI acceptance.
requirements.rationale: The acceptance target is the real browser flow and its origin/cookie behavior.

requirements.statement: Focused unit/integration tests MUST verify Jellyfin request paths, stable authorization headers, secret non-disclosure, ten-minute/single-use semantics, rate limits, immutable identity binding, separate URL validation, sanitized errors, and rendered chart/network/release contracts before deployment.
requirements.rationale: Security properties require deterministic regression coverage independent of live services.

requirements.statement: The setup UI SHOULD show a clear pending/approved/expired/canceled/error state, approval instructions linking to the fixed Jellyfin browser destination, a retry action that creates a new flow, and no page navigation during polling.
requirements.rationale: Users need actionable feedback without seeing protocol secrets.

requirements.statement: Release and rollout MUST pin Youtarr to an immutable image digest, run focused/full tests and Helm validation, deploy first to a VPN-only canary, verify health and Playwright acceptance, and provide a fail-closed rollback to the prior digest without changing Jellyfin state.
requirements.rationale: Authentication changes are high-risk and must be promoted with an auditable, reversible GitOps process.

acceptance_criteria.scenario: Given a fresh setup session, When the Jellyfin card renders, Then Quick Connect is the primary action, password fallback is secondary, no editable server URL field exists, and the page explains where to approve the code.

Given chart values with distinct internal and browser URLs, When configuration and Helm templates are validated, Then only the internal URL reaches controller environment, only the validated browser URL reaches the public UI contract, invalid URLs fail closed, and ingress/network policy is VPN-only.

Given Quick Connect is enabled, When Playwright starts a login, Then the controller calls official Initiate with stable client/device headers, the UI shows a six-character code and fixed Jellyfin link, and browser HTML, JavaScript, JSON, cookies, logs, and traces contain no Secret.

Given a pending flow, When Playwright remains on the setup page and the user approves the code in Jellyfin, Then same-origin polling transitions to approved without page redirect and creates the session only after server-side AuthenticateWithQuickConnect succeeds.

Given a pending flow, When ten minutes elapse, cancel is selected, the browser closes, or the flow is polled twice after completion, Then the flow is expired/canceled/single-use as applicable, no session is created from stale state, and the UI offers a safe retry.

Given repeated initiate, poll, cancel, or password requests from one client, When the configured limit is exceeded, Then the server returns sanitized rate-limit responses with bounded Retry-After and never reveals upstream details or secrets.

Given Jellyfin user A approves a code, When AuthenticateWithQuickConnect returns, Then Youtarr binds the session to immutable jellyfin:A-id, does not use a mutable name, and exposes only A's setup projection and data.

Given users A and B have separate sessions and CSRF cookies, When each polls, disconnects, or requests status with the other user's cookie/state, Then the request is rejected or returns only its own projection, CSRF mismatches are rejected, and no cross-user data is observable.

Given Quick Connect is unavailable or the user chooses password fallback, When Playwright submits username and password without any URL field, Then the controller authenticates only against the configured internal endpoint, clears password material, binds immutable user ID, and persists no password or reusable Jellyfin token.

Given missing, malformed, disabled, unreachable, unauthorized, or malformed Jellyfin upstream responses, When any setup flow is exercised, Then the UI shows a generic recoverable error, no raw response or target URL leaks, and no partial session or flow remains usable.

Given the release candidate, When focused/full Youtarr tests, chart lint/template, policy tests, immutable image checks, canary rollout, and rollback rehearsal run, Then all pass with explicit digest, health, VPN-only ingress, and prior-version rollback evidence.

Given a VPN-connected Playwright browser and deployed canary, When the complete Quick Connect and fallback scenarios run, Then Playwright records passing code/link/polling/session/isolation assertions and no non-Playwright browser validation is accepted as a substitute.

test_plan.approach: Test strict internal/browser URL parsing, scheme/host/path policy, fixed link construction, secret-free response projection, config startup rejection, and chart values-to-environment mapping.

Use a fake Jellyfin HTTP server to assert Initiate, Connect, and AuthenticateWithQuickConnect paths, stable X-Emby-Authorization values, response field handling, and absence of Secret from all public projections and sanitized errors.
Test opaque flow/session hashing, user binding, ten-minute boundary, single-use consumption, cancel, wrong-session rejection, CSRF matching, cookie flags, and each per-operation limiter bucket.

Exercise approved, pending, disabled, timeout, malformed, restart, duplicate, stale, wrong-user, and password-fallback state machines against fake Jellyfin and SQLite, asserting immutable IDs and no durable passwords/tokens.

Run Go focused/full tests, static secret/log scans, OpenAPI contract checks, Helm lint/template, NetworkPolicy/ingress assertions, image digest/release metadata checks, and GitOps diff/rollback contract tests.

Use Playwright only through the VPN-only deployed ingress. Verify primary Quick Connect UI, fixed browser link, code display, no page redirect during polling, user approval in Jellyfin, completion, secret non-disclosure in DOM/network/storage, and safe retry.

Use two isolated Playwright browser contexts/users to verify CSRF, expiry/cancel/reuse, rate-limit UI, session logout/restart behavior, and that neither context can observe the other's user identity or setup data.

Use Playwright only to choose password fallback with no URL input, assert generic errors and success, inspect browser-visible state for cleared password, and verify canary health plus rollback/recovery flow.

Review generated chart, Argo application, VPN/Tailscale route, secret references, immutable image digest, rollout/rollback runbook, and release provenance before promotion; manual review cannot replace browser acceptance.

review_checks: Inspect setup HTML and UI state machine for primary/default actions and absence of server URL input.
validation_checks: Playwright fresh-session assertion passes with Quick Connect primary and password secondary.

review_checks: Audit all Jellyfin client construction and outbound target selection.
validation_checks: Invalid internal configuration fails startup and no request target comes from browser input.

review_checks: Review safe URL parser, fixed link projection, and redirect policy.
validation_checks: Playwright sees only configured safe browser URL; internal host is absent from UI/network projection.

review_checks: Compare request path/header names and stable device identity with official Jellyfin contract.
validation_checks: Fake server observes exact Initiate path and stable headers across retries.

review_checks: Search response serializers, logs, errors, telemetry, cookies, and static assets for secret flows.
validation_checks: Unit secret scan and Playwright DOM/network/storage assertions pass.

review_checks: Audit flow cookie flags, hash binding, same-origin route, and no client secret state.
validation_checks: Polling with wrong or absent flow cookie is rejected; valid flow stays on page.

review_checks: Review pending/authenticated/expired/error mapping and upstream sanitization.
validation_checks: Fake upstream and Playwright approval scenarios reach only safe terminal states.

review_checks: Check ten-minute boundary, atomic consumption, cancel cleanup, and limiter keys.
validation_checks: Expired/reuse/rate-limit assertions pass for both API and Playwright contexts.

review_checks: Verify no automatic approval and only server-side Secret reaches final auth endpoint.
validation_checks: Approval in Jellyfin is required before immutable user session creation.

review_checks: Audit every read/write predicate and session transition for immutable Jellyfin ID.
validation_checks: Two-user Playwright isolation and store assertions pass.

review_checks: Inspect fallback payload, memory lifetime, logs, and UI clear behavior.
validation_checks: Password fallback succeeds only against internal URL and leaves no password/token persistence.

review_checks: Review CSRF on every mutating setup route and cookie attributes.
validation_checks: Mismatched CSRF and expired session fail safely in Playwright contexts.

review_checks: Map every lifecycle/error branch to cleanup, generic error, and retry behavior.
validation_checks: Restart, close, stale, malformed, disabled, and rate-limit cases have deterministic safe outcomes.

review_checks: Audit chart/config/NetworkPolicy/ingress/secret references and environment separation.
validation_checks: Helm/GitOps/VPN policy tests pass with no plaintext credential or internal URL browser exposure.

review_checks: Reject non-Playwright browser evidence as acceptance substitute.
validation_checks: VPN-only Playwright suite passes all browser-facing scenarios.

review_checks: Trace each security and lifecycle invariant to a focused regression test.
validation_checks: Focused/full test, static scan, and chart contract gates pass.

review_checks: Review accessible sanitized status text and retry/cancel affordances.
validation_checks: Playwright observes actionable pending/approved/expired/error UI without protocol secret.

review_checks: Audit immutable digest, canary order, health gate, rollback, and release evidence.
validation_checks: Canary Playwright/health gates pass and rollback restores prior digest without Jellyfin mutation.

perspectives.summary: Server-orchestrated Quick Connect default, explicit fallback, fixed link, and staged GitOps delivery.
Server-only secret, opaque state, immutable user binding, strict URLs, CSRF, rate limits, no logging/persistence.
Focused state-machine coverage and VPN-only Playwright browser acceptance with two-user isolation.
Official 10.11 Initiate, Connect, Authorize, and AuthenticateWithQuickConnect contract with stable headers and six-character code.

council.consensus_summary: Use a ten-minute single-use server-side Quick Connect flow. Return only a code and fixed validated browser link, poll same-origin using opaque state, require explicit Jellyfin approval, then bind an immutable Jellyfin ID. Keep password fallback internal-only and remove editable URL input. Ship only through immutable digest GitOps canary and Playwright VPN acceptance.
open_questions: Implementation must confirm the exact stable device ID derivation and Jellyfin 10.11 response casing against the deployed server during code/test stages; it must remain deterministic and non-secret.

Implementation must choose whether the flow secret is stored as a keyed hash or encrypted ciphertext based on the existing store encryption facilities; either choice must prevent database-only replay and never expose plaintext.
